drivingQuestion: Does the prohibition of the sciatic nerve apply to a non-kosher animal?
outcomeNote: The packet contains only the mishna lemma that opens the gemara's treatment; nothing is settled within it.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא מִבְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב [וְכוּ׳].
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «Rabbi Yehuda said» in explanation: «Wasn’t» the sciatic nerve forbidden for «the children of Jacob,» as it is written: “Therefore the children of Israel eat not the sciatic nerve” (Genesis 32:33), yet the meat of a non-kosher animal was still permitted to them? Since the sciatic nerve of non-kosher animals became forbidden at that time, it remains forbidden now.

moves.summary: Rabbi Yehuda presses the Sages: the nerve was forbidden already from the children of Jacob, at a time when non-kosher meat was permitted to them.
moves.about: Rabbi Yehuda argues against the Sages that since the sciatic nerve was already forbidden in the days of the children of Jacob, when non-kosher animals were still permitted to them, the prohibition must apply to a non-kosher animal too
